data.title: Border preview 2x-scaled box + upscaled 2x/4x nearest-neighbor export

data.body:
Human-requested, decisions confirmed in interview:
(1) BORDER PREVIEW: add a fifth sample box to border mode showing the border pixel-doubled — border-width = 2*cellSize, border-image slice stays cellSize, repeat mode 'repeat'. Label 'repeat 2x'. Same sheet, drawn at double pixel size. (Explicitly NOT a tile-preview change; mode 2's 1x/4x swatches stay as they are.)
(2) UPSCALED EXPORT: export PNG at 1x/2x/4x original size, nearest-neighbor so the pixel look survives when used for larger UI elements. Exposed as a small scale stepper (1x/2x/4x) beside the export key in the transport row, matching the existing cell-size stepper vocabulary; LCD shows the resulting output pixel size. One export key; the current scale applies.
Planner must decide: whether the copied CSS snippet reflects the chosen export scale (slice would become scale*cellSize for border mode; background-size for tile), and how scale interacts with the data-URI previews (previews should stay 1x - they are live CSS, not exports).

Implemented in the plan's six steps, one commit each (4c6e4bd, b77fe8b, 9d9704b, 164da84, 0fc2433, 24af51b, plus b544b0e whitespace tidy).

1. raster/buffer.ts: scaleUp(b, factor) over resizeNearest; factor<=1 returns the same buffer.
2. border-preview.ts + app.css: fifth full-width 'repeat 2x' study, border-width 2C against a 1C slice, size max(158, 4C+64); .bp-item-wide { grid-column: 1/-1 } and min-width:0 on .bp-grid. tile-preview.ts untouched.
3. store.ts exportScale: 1|2|4 (session-only, init always 1, ignores restore) + lcd.ts 'out' segment between cell and focus (plain span / orange b idiom) + main.ts outputSize() and the lcd.sync wiring.
4. transport.ts is now a spec object { onAction, onScaleStep } with sync({exportScale}); .t-group/.t-scale CSS; main.ts stepScale uses plain store.set (NOT bumpDoc) so it bumps neither dirtyDoc nor dirtyPreview.
5. png.ts downloadPNG(b, scale=1) via scaleUp; doExportPng tips 'pattern.png' / 'pattern.png Nx'.
6. css.ts second param renamed cellSize -> unit with the image-pixel doc comment; tile comment now '${unit}px is 1:1'; doCopyCss builds the URI from scaleUp(activeBuffer,...) and passes unit = C*S.

Verification: npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build clean after every step. No browser available, so pure logic was smoke-tested in a scratchpad harness (not committed):
- scaleUp: factor 1 returns the identical object; for 1x1/3x3/5x2/16x16/48x48 at 2x and 4x every output pixel equals src[floor(x/S)][floor(y/S)] and dims are exact; an isolated pixel at 4x is a hard 4x4 block of one RGBA with zero non-transparent fringe; border sheets give 48/96/192 (C=16), 576 (C=48 @4x), 768 (C=64 @4x).
- CSS snippets: captured the pre-change output before editing css.ts and diffed. At S=1 the border snippet is byte-identical for C=1/3/16/48/64; the tile snippet differs only in the trailing comment, as planned. At S=1/2/4 the border slice always equals C*S and border-width matches it; tile background-size is 4*unit.
- stepScale/outputSize traces match the plan's tables (1->2->4, clamp tips both ends; out 001x001 / 048x048 / 064x064 / 192x192 / 768x768).

Code-verified acceptance criteria: 1 (build clean); 8 and 9 (export dims + nearest-neighbor exactness, via scaleUp harness); 10 (S=1 byte-identical border snippet, tile differs only in comment — diffed against captured baseline); 12's mechanism (grep confirms nothing under preview/ reads exportScale or scaleUp, and stepScale bumps no dirty counter, so neither the preview subscriber nor the autosave subscriber fires); 13's mechanism (persist.ts untouched, no schema change, store init pins 1); 14's mechanism (no other action writes exportScale; grep lists every reader).

Needs a browser to confirm: 2, 3 (2x box crispness under image-rendering: pixelated in two engines), 4 (computed 320px at C=64), 5, 6 (layout/key travel/focus rings), 7 (LCD colours), 11 (paste the 2x snippet onto a 158px div — note the emitted keyword is 'round' as before; the criterion's 'repeat' is the documented swap), 15 (brand audit).

Deviations: none. Files listed as untouched (persist.ts, history.ts, doc.ts, editor/, compose.ts, tile-preview.ts) are confirmed untouched by git diff. One extra commit (b544b0e) removes a stray blank line I introduced in the store init.

Risk note for the reviewer: the fifth preview box and the export scale are deliberately independent — the box doubles CSS drawing size against a 1x raster at every scale, and never reads exportScale.

REVIEW (cold, fresh context) — VERDICT: PASS, no rework needed. Moving to done.

Scope reviewed: 4c6e4bd, b77fe8b, 9d9704b, 164da84, 0fc2433, 24af51b, b544b0e (c1f75a0 = lattice state). Read the full current text of all 9 modified files plus the untouched neighbours they lean on (dom.ts, toolbar.ts, compose.ts, doc.ts, persist.ts, store.ts).

MECHANICAL
- npx tsc --noEmit: 0 errors. npm run build: passes (34 modules, 37.26 kB js / 7.77 kB css).
- npm run dev serves 200 on / and /src/main.ts. (Note: vite found 5173 already occupied by a leftover server and took 5174; my cleanup killed both. No repo state touched, working tree clean, dist/ is gitignored. Restart dev if you had one open.)
- Wrote my OWN two harnesses in scratchpad (not committed, nothing added to the repo): a pure-logic one over scaleUp + the css generators (transpiled sources, plus `git show 6b119c3:src/export/css.ts` as the pre-change oracle), and a stubbed-DOM one that instantiates createTransport / createLcd / createBorderPreview for real. ~160 assertions, all pass.

THE THINGS MOST LIKELY TO BE SUBTLY WRONG — checked independently, all correct
- Border slice math: derived from the raster rather than the code. Sheet = 3·C·S; a third of it is C·S; borderCSS emits slice = unit = C·S and border-width = unit px. Verified for C ∈ {1,2,16,17,48,64} × S ∈ {1,2,4} that 3 × emitted-slice reconstructs the sheet exactly. The garbage-snippet failure mode is not present.
- S=1 byte-identity: borderCSS(uri, C) === pre-change borderCSS(uri, C) character-for-character at C ∈ {1,3,16,31,48,64}. tileCSS differs on exactly one line, and is identical once comments are stripped — i.e. only the trailing comment moved, as specified.
- scaleUp is exact NN: for every (w,h) × S tested, every destination pixel equals src[floor(x/S)][floor(y/S)] with zero mismatches. Isolated-pixel test (criterion 9) gives exactly a 16-px block of ONE distinct RGBA and zero non-transparent pixels anywhere outside it — no fringe. factor<=1 returns the *same object* (identity, no copy), and the source is not mutated by writes to the result.
- exportScale is session-only: grep shows it in store.ts, main.ts, transport.ts only — never in persist.ts/history.ts, and store init hardcodes `exportScale: 1` ignoring `restored`. stepScale uses plain store.set and touches neither dirtyDoc nor dirtyPreview; traced both subscriptions in main.ts (preview sub keys on dirtyPreview/mode/dirtyDoc, autosave sub on dirtyDoc/dirtyPreview/mode/colorHex) — a scale step matches none of them, so no preview regeneration and no autosave churn. Criterion 12's mechanism is real, not incidental.
- Nothing under preview/ reads exportScale (grep for store/state/AppState in src/preview/ returns nothing). Previews stay 1×.
- 2× box formula: max(158, 4·C+64) intact. Verified C=1/16/23→158, 24→160, 32→192, 48→256, 64→320, and that the content strip is >=64px at every C so box-sizing:border-box can never inflate the used width. 320px fits the 440px .output column — no overflow, no page scroll.
- image-rendering: pixelated really reaches the box: the 2× div carries className 'bp-box' (asserted in the DOM harness), and .bp-box sets it. Inline width/height beat the .bp-box 158px rule (inline > stylesheet), so they don't fight.
- Transport factory change: DOM harness confirms the row is exactly undo redo clear save load css [scale] export, and that every one of the 7 keys still routes through spec.onAction (no call site dropped). minus/plus emit -1/+1; sync(1|2|4) writes 1×/2×/4×.
- LCD out segment sits between cell and focus; plain <span> vs orange <b> with exactly one visible at a time. Extremes verified: tile/C=1/S=1 → 001×001, border/C=64/S=4 → 768×768, border 3·C·S vs tile C·S per mode. Never more than 3 digits, so no jitter.
- Clamping: 1× minus stays 1×, 4× plus stays 4×, no wrap even at delta ±5; tips fire only on the no-op branch.
- CSS specificity: .t-scale .key / .t-scale .readout (lines 353-354) and .stepper .key / .stepper .readout (166-181) are equal specificity, and the .t-scale rules come later, so they win. Crucially .t-group > span uses the child combinator, so it styles only the 'scale' label and does NOT hit the .readout nested inside .stepper.t-scale — that was the trap and it's avoided. .stepper button.readout{cursor:text} correctly misses the inert <span>.
- Untouched-by-design confirmed empty diff: persist.ts, history.ts, doc.ts, editor/, compose.ts, tile-preview.ts. No PM-7 / PM-6 / PM-4 regression surface: toolbar.ts and the .stepper rules are byte-unchanged, and the only shared CSS edit is .transport{align-items:end}, which is a genuine no-op (t-key = 34+3+~11 ≈ 48px, t-group = 34+3+~11 ≈ 48px).
- scaleUp worst case (192→768) runs in ~1.2 ms for 590k px / 2.3 MB, on the export path only.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1 build clean — verified-by-build. 2 five boxes / labels — verified-by-code (DOM harness). 3 158px + bw 32 + slice 16 at C=16, art exactly 2× — geometry verified-by-code; visual crispness cannot-verify-without-browser. 4 computed 320px at C=64, no overflow — verified-by-code. 5 tile preview unchanged — verified-by-code (zero diff). 6 row order, stepping, clamp tips — verified-by-code; key travel/rings cannot-verify-without-browser. 7 out segment values + orange — verified-by-code (all five cases). 8 export dimensions — verified-by-code (64/192/192/576/16/48). 9 nearest-neighbor, no fringe — verified-by-code. 10 S=1 byte-identity — verified-by-code. 11 pasted 2× snippet matches the preview box — verified-by-math (both draw a C-image-px corner into 2C css px); the actual paste is cannot-verify-without-browser. Testing note for whoever does it: the snippet emits 'round', so swap it to 'repeat' before comparing against the repeat 2× box, otherwise you are comparing two different repeat modes. 12 previews unchanged at 2×/4× — verified-by-code (subscription trace). 13/14 session-only, survives undo/mode/cell/focus/load — verified-by-code. 15 brand audit — verified-by-code against BRANDING.md (9px lowercase mono --label on the 'scale' label and 'repeat 2×'; readout stays --lcd-text charcoal at every scale; only new orange is the LCD out value at S>1; no new colour outside the token set; prefers-reduced-motion block untouched).

FINDINGS
No defects. No inline fixes were needed and nothing was changed — the diff is exactly what the plan specified, including the two hazards the plan called out by name (slice-scales-with-raster, and the border-box size formula).

Two observations, neither blocking, recorded for the next mind rather than as rework:
(a) The scale readout is a <span> carrying aria-label; aria-label on a role=generic element is not reliably exposed by AT. It doesn't matter much here because the live-region announcement reads the content ('2×') and the wrapping .t-group already has role=group + aria-label='export scale'. It also exactly mirrors the existing cell readout idiom, so changing it unilaterally would break the vocabulary. Leave it.
(b) transport.sync/lcd.sync rewrite textContent on every store.set (including hover moves), which touches an aria-live region with identical text. Pre-existing pattern from the cell readout; browsers diff live regions by text, so in practice silent. Flagged only so it isn't rediscovered as new.

The remaining unverifiable items are all single-question visual confirmations in Chrome + Firefox/Safari: that pixelated is honoured on border-image for the 2× box (plan §5 already names the fallback and says raise rather than improvise), and that stepping the scale produces no preview flicker (the code path says it cannot).
